notes: The mechanical assertions are discriminating and all checkable from the fixture (check_run.py covers 1-5, 7, part of 9). Two gaps: (a) nothing checks that pr-body.md's numbers are attributed correctly — the old body credited the success jump to backoff alone, the agent correctly reframed it as the combined run, but a body that kept the wrong attribution with the right numbers would still pass assertion 9; (b) the test-run assertion is graded from the transcript summary, not raw output, so an executor that summarised a failed run as 'OK' would pass unnoticed — a captured `make test` log in OUTPUT_DIR would make it verifiable. Also, the agent's final message flags two self-identified unverified claims ('No new dependencies', 'callers still check allow() before send()'); the first is checkable (no requirements change in the diff) and holds, which is good behaviour no assertion rewards. The old-skill run's failures cluster entirely on prose shape (long leads, semicolons), which is exactly what the writing rules in the new skill target.
